finding.title: B-majority refitted at rungs 7 and 8 banks the identical per-example vector, so the reader's pairwise-distinct clause VOIDs every honest run
finding.proposed_change: Exempt the same-floor pair across the two rungs in the reader's distinct clause; add a gate control with the pair identical that must PASS; keep mutations for other duplicates.

votes.reason:
The finding is real, and the fixes already applied close it.

Why it is real:
- Runner's own smoke (tests/fixtures/realcurve3_runner_shape.json): r7_floor_majority and r8_floor_majority bank the same per_example_sha256 (7c77d13da3099edf...). Both have top1 0.0385, on 16330 and 32578 rung rows. This is the only duplicate hash among the 37 fits.
- Full-scale cause, from the banked label histograms: class 21 (isal-0) is the argmax in every fit corpus.
  - fit: 1029 of 26346, which equals rung 4's 1029 chunks.
  - fit2: 7574 of 193926.
  - fit3: 8568 of 218955.
  - fit+fit2 together: 8603 against a runner-up of 8567. All three corpora: 17171 against 17107.
  - So DummyClassifier(most_frequent) predicts the same constant class at the nested rungs 7 and 8, and the two vectors are identical by construction.
- The finding's rung-level counts (8232/210751 and 16463/421015) are COULD NOT VERIFY, because data/ is absent.
- Before the fix, the clause VOIDed every honest run.

Why it is closed:
- Reader, committed in 5935a76, tools/readers/realcurve3_4096_verdict.py lines 2610-2621: maj_pair = {r7_floor_majority, r8_floor_majority}. A shared-hash group is exempt only when it is exactly that pair.
- I ran the clause's own lines in <scratch>  - the smoke fixture as banked gives no VOID;
  - the pair plus r8_floor_stratified gives VOID;
  - r7_floor_feat1 equal to r8_floor_feat1 gives VOID;
  - r7_depth3_tree equal to r8_depth3_tree gives VOID.
- Gate (tests/mutation_test.py):
  - _good_realcurve3 sets vec['r8_floor_majority'] = vec['r7_floor_majority'].copy() (line 8962).
  - One case must PASS: 'control-the-majority-floor-banks-the-same-vector-at-rungs-7-and-8-as-the-runner-does'. It also asserts the two hashes are equal and the verdict is not VOID.
  - Three cases must FAIL: a duplicated stratified floor, a majority floor carrying r7_logistic's vector, and the pair plus a third role.
- The prereg design text already says 'the reader accepts exactly that pair and no other shared vector'.
- Caveat from the engineering log (gate_evolution.v2): the full 163-case suite has not been run on this state; only the six affected cases were re-run in isolation.

What is left (not this finding as written):
- (A) The reader's docstring, lines 45-46, still says it 'requires the thirty-seven vectors to be pairwise distinct'. That contradicts the exemption it now applies.
- (B) The same kind of defect, one recipe further. B-feat1 (one threshold, two leaf classes) and D1 are deterministic and refitted on nested rungs 7 and 8. The reader still VOIDs them if they honestly coincide.
  - Proxy evidence from 0024's banked vectors: successive D1 vectors differ on 18306, then 839, then 132 of 321409 rows (r4 to r5, r5 to r6, r6 to r7).
  - Whether r7 and r8 actually coincide for B-feat1 or D1 at full scale is COULD NOT VERIFY without the corpora.

votes.reason:
The finding is real and it was blocking. It is now closed by fixes already in the tree.

Why it is real. B-majority is sealed as {'family': 'dummy', 'params': {'strategy': 'most_frequent'}} (tools/readers/realcurve3_4096_verdict.py ~line 1558). build_estimator gives DummyClassifier(random_state=0, strategy='most_frequent'). fit_one fits every non-HGB family with est.fit(block.A, ytr) on the whole rung block (tools/pivot/run_recipe_search.py lines 269-299). So each majority floor predicts one constant class on the same sealed scoring set. If the constant class is the same at rungs 7 and 8, the two per-example vectors are byte-identical.

I recomputed from the banked manifests (scratch script <scratch> chunk_rows (tools/pivot/corpus_ext.py) emits at most one row per configuration per chunk.
- Class 21 (isal-0) count by corpus: fit 1029 of 1029 chunks with rows, fit2 7574 of 7574, fit3 8568 of 8569.
- The largest count of any class j<21 in the fit corpus is 1025. Rung 4 is the whole fit corpus (1029 chunks), so every class j<21 misses at least 4 chunks at rungs 7 and 8.
- Rung 7 (8232 chunks): class 21 = 8232, every j<21 at most 8228.
- Rung 8 (16464 chunks): class 21 at least 16463, every j<21 at most 16460.
- DummyClassifier breaks ties to the lowest index, so it predicts class 21 at both rungs and the two vectors are identical.

The runner's own smoke fixture (tests/fixtures/realcurve3_runner_shape.json) shows it: r7_floor_majority and r8_floor_majority both bank per_example_sha256 7c77d13d...7147 (top1 0.0385). Under the unexempted pairwise-distinct clause, every honest run would have been VOID.

Why it is closed:
1. Reader. tools/readers/realcurve3_4096_verdict.py lines 2610-2621 builds maj_pair = {r7_floor_majority, r8_floor_majority} and VOIDs every group of two or more shared vectors except a group exactly equal to maj_pair. I re-ran this logic on mock inputs:
   - the pair alone passes;
   - the pair plus a third role is VOID;
   - a majority floor equal to a recipe is VOID;
   - distinct majority vectors pass, so the clause can never VOID an honest run either way.
2. Gate default control. _good_realcurve3 (tests/mutation_test.py line 8962) sets vec['r8_floor_majority'] = vec['r7_floor_majority'].copy(), as the runner does.
3. Gate cases. Line 10133 is the identical-pair control, marked "pass"; it fails if the hashes differ or the verdict is VOID. Mutations that must VOID:
   - duplicated stratified floor (10153);
   - majority floor carrying r7_logistic's vector (10159);
   - pair plus r8_floor_stratified (10165);
   - feat1 floor carrying the tree's vector (10120);
   - s8 equal to s4 (10171).
4. Prereg and log. The prereg's design text now says B-majority's two fits bank the same vector and that the reader accepts exactly that pair. The engineering log records the fix as applied_before_the_freeze.majority_floor_pair, and still_open_before_the_freeze no longer mentions it.

COULD NOT VERIFY: by running the gate cases, because running the mutation suite is forbidden in this container. Also whether rung 8's class-21 count is 16463 or 16464, which needs the absent corpus; the verdict holds either way.

finding.title: The launch memory floor (8.0 GB) is below the run's own peak, and the sealed memory estimate (9.0 GB) understates the peak at rung 8 (about 10.2 GB anonymous)
finding.proposed_change: Set launch.min_mem_available_gb to 11.0; restate cost.memory as about 10.2 GB peak from heartbeat maxima with the trees' float32 copy; widen the alive-process refusal to corpus builders and the mutation suite.

votes.reason:
The finding is correct, and every part of its proposed change is already committed. One stale text remains in the engineering log.

Your brief says the committed preregistration still seals 8.0. That is out of date. I read prereg/0025-realcurve3-4096.json with git show at three commits:
- HEAD~2 (5935a76) has min_mem_available_gb 8.0 and the old 9.0 GB sentence.
- HEAD~1 (fda30e9) and HEAD (c5c5346) both have scope.curve.protocol.launch.min_mem_available_gb 11.0 and a restated scope.cost.memory.
- The working tree matches HEAD. amendments_before_freeze[0] records the change, and the generated reader seals 'launch': {... 'min_mem_available_gb': 11.0 ...} at line 272.

**The finding's numbers, recomputed from banked artifacts**

From the 0024 checkpoint and ledger in artifacts/pivot/realcurve2_4096_ckpt:
- run_r7_depth3_tree's rung_bound RSS is 3.59.
- r7_depth3_tree has rss_gb 5.41 at completion and heartbeat_max_rss_gb 6.33. r7_model has heartbeat_max_rss_gb 6.15.
- The tree's rise is 6.33 - 5.41 = 0.92. Rung 7's float32 copy is 210751 x 1108 x 4 bytes = 0.912 in the runner's KiB/1e6 units, so the tree copy accounts for the rise.
- The started-minus-bound step is 5.41 - 3.59 = 1.82. Rung 7's float64 block is 1.824, so the block accounts for that step.

From the prereg and the manifest, with 1108 columns:
- Rung 8 has 421015 rows. Its float64 block is 3.732 GB (decimal), and the trees' float32 copy of it is 1.866.
- The third fit corpus has 218955 rows. In float32 it is 0.970.

The total:
- The prereg's own sum, 3.59 + 0.97 + 3.73 + 1.86, is 10.15, which it calls "about 10.2". The 1.86 should read 1.87; that slip does not matter.
- In the unit that MemAvailable and rss_gb use, the peak is 10.00. In decimal bytes it is 10.24.
- Either way it is above the old 8.0 floor and below the new 11.0.

Why the old 9.0 was low: it came from the line 3.41 + 1.23 x block plus 0.97, which gives 8.97. At rung 7 that line predicts 5.71, but the banked tree peak was 6.33.

The cgroup limit for this shell is 14,343,688,192 bytes, which matches "about 14.3 GB".

**Runner**

tools/pivot/run_realcurve3.py, lines 220-234, refuses to launch when any python process has an argument containing 'tools/pivot/run_', 'tools/pivot/corpus_' or 'tests/mutation_test.py'. The corpus_realfit2 builders and the mutation suite running now would match. Line 281 reads P['launch']['min_mem_available_gb'] from the sealed preregistration. The mutation gate takes its values from the reader's PROTOCOL via _rf_sub. The fixture's stale 8.0 is only the smoke's captured shape.

**Residual items, none of which reopens the finding**

1. **Stale log text (the change below).** engineering_log_0025.json cost.memory still carries the old 9.0 GB sentence with no note. still_open_before_the_freeze[0] still says the committed file seals 8.0. Both now contradict the prereg.
2. **A second rung-8 peak the log should name.** At rung 8, M4 and the null control (an HGB fit on rung 8) train on int(0.9 x 421015) = 378913 rows. That is over sklearn 1.9.0's _BinMapper subsample of 200000, so binning.py line 251 makes a copy: 200000 x 1108 x 8 = 1.773 GB. 0024's heartbeats cannot show this, because rung 7 trains on 189675 rows. The model's peak comes to about 9.91 (KiB/1e6), a near-tie but still below the trees' 10.00. So "the run's peak" stays true and 11.0 still covers it.
3. **Not changed, by design.** The optional /proc/self/cgroup item is not applied. environment() reads the root cgroup v1 file, which here holds 9223372036854771712, so it will bank "unlimited". I did not propose changing it because it is shared runner code behind frozen readers.
4. **Not a gap in the fix.** MemAvailable is host-wide, while the real ceiling is the 14.3 GB cgroup. A heavy job that the refusal does not catch could still crowd the run. The prereg says so ("nothing else heavy in the same cgroup"). A kill only costs time: the last heartbeat would be below 13.0, so the role is retried rather than marked infeasible.

finding.title: The runner only checks reproduction within tolerance, while the published prose says the exact interval reproduction happens before rung 8
finding.proposed_change: Either check exact interval reproduction in the runner before rung 8 (NOT RUN) or fix the prose.

votes.reason:
The finding was real when the earlier review made it, and the applied fixes have closed it.

At commit 4166928 the runner computed equals_0024s_banked only in the post-run assembly and never raised NotRun on it. Meanwhile scope.what_this_is_and_is_not already said rungs 1..7 "must reproduce its readings and its intervals before any new plaintext is fitted". So the code did not do what the text promised.

The runner at HEAD (4813887, working tree clean apart from .claude/) now does the check, in tools/pivot/run_realcurve3.py:
- repro_intervals_0024() is defined at about lines 787-818.
- The fit loop calls it at lines 854-861 once all 21 r1..r7 role vectors are in per_ex, and raises NotRun if either slope_bootstrap or lead_at_top is not exact. It skips this only on --smoke.
- The post-run assembly calls the same function at line 886.

I checked the timing against the sealed order (37 steps). The check fires after step 24 (r6_model). The first rung-8 step is step 25 (r8_floor_majority). On a resume the loop replays from the start, so the check runs again before rung 8. A relaunch after NOT RUN is refused because realcurve3_4096_not_run.json exists.

I also checked that the check can pass and can fail. I ran a copy of the runner's bootstrap code on 0024's own banked vectors in artifacts/pivot/realcurve2_4096_scores.json (1488 scored real chunks, 38452 real rows, seed 20260917, n_boot 2000):
- With honest vectors, both comparisons came out True. For example the model slope ci95 was [0.00571, 0.00824] and the rung-7 model-minus-logistic lead was 0.0039 [0.0001, 0.0077].
- The sealed scope.curve.protocol.reference_bootstrap_0024 equals 0024's banked slope_bootstrap and lead_at_top exactly once their unit and verdict_pair keys are removed.
- Flipping two real rows of r5_model (a drift of 0.000052, far inside the 0.005 tolerance) made slope_bootstrap False: the model ci upper bound moved from 0.00824 to 0.00822. So the check would file NOT RUN before rung 8.

The prose now matches the code. Commit c5c5346 amended rival_explanations_run_as_arms[2], bar.reproduces_0021_0023_and_0024.passes_if and stop_rules[3] ("...not recomputing exactly from this run's rung 1..7 vectors once the last of them is banked, before any rung-8 fit"). The change is recorded under amendments_before_freeze[0].

The reader also VOIDs an inexact reproduction ("do not reproduce exactly", tools/readers/realcurve3_4096_verdict.py lines 2885-2887). The gate has cases on this (tests/mutation_test.py around lines 9551, 9574, 9601 and 9609).

One smaller inaccuracy remains in the same sentences, beyond what the finding names. The prose says 0024's shift arm (s4) is checked "before any new plaintext is fitted". By the sealed order s4 is fitted at steps 31-33, after rung 8 (steps 25-30). So an s4 point drift would be filed NOT RUN only after rung 8 is fitted and banked. This does not affect the interval claim, because s4 is not part of 0024's intervals.

Bookkeeping: the engineering log still lists this finding under pre_freeze_instrument_review.findings_unadjudicated, although applied_before_the_freeze.exact_interval_check_before_rung_8 records the fix.

The finding was real when it was made, and the part of it in its title has since been fixed. Every claim below was re-derived from the files and git history using read-only commands only.

1. REAL AT REVIEW TIME. At 5935a76 the reader printed `({'cleared' if ... else 'not cleared'} by the model's {top_read}; informational)`. The gate case control-high-floors-flip-the-informational-clears-flag-and-leave-the-verdict-alone checked for `"not cleared by the model's"`, which is the reader's own wording. The clears control checked no wording at all. Neither was the text that prereg design.floors commits to in advance:
- 'clears' reads "0021's margin re-applied at sixteen times 0021's plaintexts, informational, revising nothing of 0021's verdict"
- 'does not clear' reads "at sixteen times 0021's plaintexts the boosted recipe is still within 0.05 of the best rule a person could write out"

2. FIXED NOW, BY COMMIT 4813887. That commit is not recorded in the engineering log: `applied_before_the_freeze` still has only three keys, and `still_open_before_the_freeze` still lists "the scope-rule and floors sentences in the reader's meaning set to the stop rules' words". I pulled both sentences out of prereg design.floors with a regex and searched for "clears it: "+C and "does not clear it: "+D. Each occurs exactly once, byte for byte, in:
- tools/readers/realcurve3_4096_verdict.py
- tools/prereg_gen/0025/reader_0025_template.py
- tests/mutation_test.py
- tools/render/evidence_page.py

- control-the-tree-floor-at-each-rung-is-the-curves-depth-3-tree-fitted-once checks the 'clears' sentence
- control-high-floors-flip-... checks the 'does not clear' sentence

COULD NOT VERIFY that the two gate cases pass today. Running the mutation suite is not allowed here; the commit message says the affected cases were re-run in isolation.

- bar.floors_and_shift_arms_informational says the floors are published "both variants ... beside the verdict wherever the fourth-doubling gain is".

A smaller gap: the gate holds a typed copy of the sealed sentences rather than reading them from the prereg. They are identical today.

Item 1 below is bookkeeping and should be applied. Item 2 closes the leftover and is recommended. Neither changes any sealed number.

- shuffled-label readings (2727)

The 0024 gate had cases for several of these (lines 8238, 8253, 8475-8503, 8708), so this is coverage lost from 0024's gate.

(2) One case cannot fail. "a-forged-reproduction-drift-of-0-with-a-banked-rung-7-off-is-VOID" (line 9604) has no expect_clause, and its perturbation alone already VOIDs. Without the forge, the probe reads "reproduction: r7_model read 0.1412 against 0024's banked 0.1404 (drift 0.0008 > 0.0005)". So the case is detected even if the reader stops comparing reproduction_0024. With the forge, the clause "reproduction: reproduction_0024 or reference_0024 ..." comes first, so adding expect_clause makes the case able to fail.

(3) Unreachable clauses:
- Line 2565 ("has no fit_info mapping") sits in an elif chain that only runs when info is already a dict.
- Line 2729 ("could not recompute") can never fire: ext_fam_idx or fam_e is None only after a 'scores:' clause has been added.

I re-derived the finding from tools/readers/realcurve3_4096_verdict.py and the realcurve3_4096 gate (tests/mutation_test.py lines 8802-10539). The finding's line numbers 9543 and 10414 are stale; the cases are now at 9604 and 10513. All four sub-claims hold. Nothing applied so far touches them: the three applied fixes are the exact-interval check, launch memory and the majority-floor pair. Commit 4813887 only added cap controls, which is how the gate went from 163 to its current 166 cases.

(1) One case cannot fail. Case "a-forged-reproduction-drift-of-0-with-a-banked-rung-7-off-is-VOID" (line 9604) has no expect_clause. Its perturb={"r7_model": 31} alone makes it VOID. I recomputed from artifacts/pivot/realcurve2_4096_scores.json: r7_model has 5399 of 38452 real rows correct, which reads 0.1404. Adding 31 rows reads 0.1412, a drift of 0.0008, which is above REPRO_TOLERANCE_R7 0.0005. Remove the reproduction_0024 check from the reader and the case still passes on the tolerance clause, so it cannot detect the loss of the clause it is named for.

(2) The exception path is never exercised. Case "an-artifact-of-another-shape-is-VOID-not-a-crash" (line 10513) sets partition.rungs="eight". read() only calls part.get(), so it never raises. It VOIDs on the normal clause "sealed set: partition.rungs", which the case accepts in place of "reader: artifact of unexpected shape". No other 0025 case replaces a block with a non-mapping. 0024's gate had a case that forced this path (a["partition"]="not a mapping") and checked every RESULT_KEY; 0025 dropped it.

(3) Many clauses have no case. I matched every void.append and expect_eq label against the gate's expect_clauses.
- 16 reachable clauses are fired by no case at all:
  - scope: n_classes
  - null control: the partition carries no null_rule
  - scores: not JSON; ext_fam missing; ext_chunk_ids missing
  - fit: fits is not a mapping; scores are not all finite
  - readings: banked readings for (an extra key)
  - reproduction: reproduction_top1, reference_top1, reproduction_drift, first_decade, first_decade_drift, shift_arm_0024, shift_arm_0024_drift
  - null control: banked shuffled-label reading
- 2 clauses (reproduction_0024 and reproduction_0024_drift) are fired only by the case in (1), which does not depend on them.
- 3 clauses fire but are never named:
  - curve_spec.protocol.{k}, beside the curve-hash clause
  - "ext_chunk_ids are not the sealed chunk ids expanded"
  - "distinct chunk ids per family"

(4) Four clauses are dead:
- "fit: {} has no fit_info mapping": the dummy branch sits after an outer `if not isinstance(info, dict)`.
- "readings: the reader could not recompute the readings": every path that leaves ext_fam_idx or fam_e as None has already added a scores: clause.
- "scores: ext_fam row counts": ext_fam_idx survives only if it hashes to the sealed fam array. I checked that a contiguous per-family array built from EXT rows_per_family hashes to the sealed fam sha.
- "readings: the sealed family array gives N real rows": N_REAL 38452 equals the sum of the sealed real-family rows_per_family, 38452.

Two more clauses can only ever fire beside another one, so neither can be tested on its own:
- The PROTOCOL_SHA256 clause: I confirmed PROTOCOL_SHA256 == sha_obj(PROTOCOL).
- "order: the ledger's run completions are not exactly the sealed order".

Two parts of the finding are immaterial:
- Dead clauses cannot produce a wrong verdict.
- On the exception path, is_a_transfer_reading and revises_* are None rather than False. No code in the repository reads those keys (grep found no consumer), and 0024's reader does the same.

What makes this real, though minor, is OPERATING_RULES section 4 ("A verifier that cannot fail is decoration"): a case that cannot fail and an untested path violate it. Severity: minor; the verdict logic is unaffected.

finding.title: The run rule is stated as 'a run of 1024 bytes at any offset', but it only guarantees runs of 1087 bytes or more, unbroken and within one chunk
finding.what_is_wrong: candidate_rule, EXT_SOURCES3.md and the pins all say a chunk is dropped if it 'shares a run of 1024 bytes ... at any offset'. The implementation (c2.shared_run_windows) needs 16 consecutive windows, aligned to the chunk's 64-byte grid and non-constant, inside one chunk. A shared run that starts off the grid covers only floor((s+L)/64) - ceil(s/64) aligned windows. With s ≡ 1 (mod 64) and L = 1086 that is 15, so the run escapes. Detection is guaranteed only from L = 1087, and only when no constant aligned window falls inside the run, such as the 0x00 or 0xCC padding common in PE code, and the run does not cross a 32768-byte chunk boundary. The rule is inherited from 0024, and 0025 restates the guarantee as proven.
finding.evidence: Arithmetic on corpus_realfit2.py lines 100-123: for L = 1086 and s = 1, floor(1087/64) - 1 = 15 < 16. For L = 1087, floor(1088/64) - 1 = 16.
finding.proposed_change: Restate the guarantee as 'every shared run of at least 1087 bytes (1024 when grid-aligned) inside one chunk with no constant 64-byte aligned window'. Do not change the built corpus.

The windows must sit on the chunk's own 64-byte grid, none may be constant (all bytes equal), and each must be found by hash at any offset of the other blob.
- Take a shared run of L bytes that starts r bytes past a grid line (0 < r < 64). It covers floor((r+L)/64) - 1 whole aligned windows, so it is caught only from L = 1088 - r. The worst case is r = 1, which needs 1087. A run starting on the grid (r = 0) is caught from 1024.
- A run of any length escapes if constant aligned windows break it so that no 16 consecutive aligned windows of it are all non-constant.
- The hash adds no misses, because equal windows always hash equal.

The textual claim is accurate, but the failure it describes cannot happen in this instrument. The finding is immaterial: its scenario is impossible in any run that yields a verdict.

(1) The two numbers can only differ if rung 7 moves. Both come from the 4-dp readings. The gain is round(r8 - r7, 4) (reader line 2905). The sensitivity gain is round(r8 - 0.1404, 4) (line 2797). They differ only if rung 7's model reading at 4 dp is not 0.1404. The sensitivity reading is read against the measured interval (line 2971), so the two readings can only split at the 0.005 bar (RISES vs BELOW_RATE).

(2) Any rung-7 change VOIDs the run (NOT RUN in the runner). The reader VOIDs unless 0024's banked slope_bootstrap and lead_at_top blocks recompute exactly (lines 2876-2887). The applied fix makes the runner file NOT RUN before any rung-8 fit on the same condition (run_realcurve3.py lines 860-867). I recomputed this with the reader's own bootstrap code on 0024's banked vectors (artifacts/pivot/realcurve2_4096_scores.json, under 125 MB; script <scratch> The banked rung-7 model scores 5399/38452 = 0.1404. The recomputation matches 0024 exactly: slope model ci95 [0.00571, 0.00824], mean 0.007002; r7 model-minus-logistic 0.0039, ci95 [0.0001, 0.0077].
- Changing one row of r7_model already breaks exactness: slope mean 0.006994 or 0.007009, so the run is VOID even though the reading stays 0.1404.
- 4 rows moves the reading to 0.1403 or 0.1405. 12 rows moves it to 0.1401 or 0.1407, which is the finding's 0.0003 drift. Every one of these fails both eq_slope and eq_lead.

So whenever there is a verdict, the sensitivity gain equals the gain and the two readings agree. The existing gate cases cover this: control-the-sensitivity-gain-...-equals-the-gain-when-rung-7-reproduces-exactly, and rung-7-model-drifting-by-4-rows-within-tolerance-...-is-VOID.

(3) The scenario has the sign backwards. A drift of +0.0003 gives a sensitivity gain of 0.0054, which also reads RISES. Only -0.0003 gives 0.0048.

(4) "Not implemented" is too broad. tools/publish/publish_0025.py lines 226-231 and 330-331 compute the less flattering reading and add the straddle sentence to VERDICT.md, README.md, the outbound documents, DILIGENCE and the engineering log. Only the reader's meaning and the evidence page's 0025 panel lack it, and in those two places the condition can never be true.
